headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Will Golden State close out WNBA Finals? How to watch Valkyries vs. Dream Game 6
headlines.description: The first elimination game of the 2026 WNBA Finals is on deck. The Golden State Valkyries have a chance to close out the Finals and secure the franchise’s first championship in Game 6 against the Atlanta Dream Thursday. And there’s a chance Valkyries fans will be celebrating a championship victory at around noon PT on a weekday. That’s because the Game 6 tipoff time was moved up so it could be played at State Farm Arena, home of the NBA‘s Atlanta Hawks. Games 3 and 4 were also played at State Farm Arena, which holds around 14,000 more fans than the Dream’s normal home venue, Gateway Center Arena in College Park. But the Hawks have a game Thursday night that couldn’t be rescheduled. The Valkyries have the Dream on the ropes after winning two straight games, turning a 2-1 series deficit into a 3-2 advantage. Golden State forced Atlanta into a combined 32 turnovers across Games 4 and 5, while Kiah Stokes and Co. limited Angel Reese to 15 total points in those contests. In a matchup between two of the WNBA’s top defenses, points have been hard to come by. Atlanta is shooting 36% from the field and 24.8% from 3-point range for the series, while Golden State is at 35.2% from the field and 26.5% from deep. So, will the Dream rebound and extend the series to a decisive Game 7? Or will the Valkyries go from expansion franchise to champions in just two seasons? Here’s how to watch Game 6 of the WNBA Finals: When is the next Valkyries vs. Dream WNBA Finals game? The Valkyries and Dream will meet in Game 6 on Thursday, Oct. 29. What time does Valkyries vs. Dream Game 6 start? Tipoff from State Farm Arena is scheduled for 12:30 p.m. ET/11:30 a.m. CT/9:30 a.m. PT. WNBA Oct 16 WNBA Oct 20 What TV channel is Valkyries vs. Dream Game 6 on? Game 6 will air across USA Network, E! and SYFY. It will also be shown on Peacock. Where to stream Valkyries vs. Dream Game 6 live online Viewers can stream Game 6 on Peacock, USANetwork.com and the USA Network app. When is Valkyries vs. Dream Game 7? If Atlanta wins, Game 7 will be played Saturday, Oct. 31 at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT/5 p.m. PT. Golden State would host the winner-take-all showdown.

headlines.title: 1-year-old girl dies after being hit by vehicle in Oakland
headlines.description: A toddler died after falling out of a moving vehicle and being run over near a church and school in Oakland Tuesday afternoon. The 1-year-old girl was hit at about 3:45 p.m. in the 3700 block of Dorisa Avenue, close to the St. Paschal Baylon Catholic Church and the Northern Light School. She was taken to a hospital, where she died, according to Oakland police, who said drugs and alcohol don’t appear to have been a factor in the collision. Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee posted condolences to the child’s family on social media. “Late this afternoon, our community suffered an unimaginable tragedy with the heartbreaking loss of a one-year-old child who fell from a moving vehicle,” Lee said in her post Tuesday. “Words cannot fully express the grief we feel for the family and loved ones during this painful time. My deepest condolences and prayers are with them, as well as with our first responders. I ask everyone in our city to hold this family in their hearts tonight.” Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact the Oakland Police Department Traffic Investigation Unit at 510-777-8570.

headlines.title: ‘Her impact was boundless': Leaders pay tribute to Dolores Huerta after her death at 96
headlines.description: Renowned labor leader, civil rights icon and feminist activist Dolores Huerta has died at 96, her family announced Wednesday. Her passing prompted leaders from across the country to pen touching tributes. Read their statements below. Dolores Huerta’s family “We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96. As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family. We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy.” Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi “Today, we sadly mourn the loss of Dolores Huerta, a leader in the American labor movement and a champion for civil rights who lead with courage and determination. Dolores was a dear friend, and we all responded to her rallying cry, ‘Sí se puede,’ which inspired generations of Americans to believe in the power of collective action. I was honored to host Dolores’ birthday celebration at the United States Capitol when she turned 90, a compliment she returned to me at the California Democratic Party Convention in San Francisco earlier this year. May it be a comfort to her family and loved ones that so many mourn their loss and are praying for them at this sad time.” California Gov. Gavin Newsom and First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom “Dolores represented the best of us. California — and the United States — would not be what we are today without her resolute spirit, her passion for justice and fairness, and her commitment to those overlooked and forgotten. Dolores started off as a teacher, working with the children of farmworkers, and although she moved away from the classroom, she never stopped teaching. As a leader in the National Farm Workers Association, and later the United Farm Workers, she fought for gender equity, workers’ rights, and civil rights, paving the way for generations to come, and teaching people what was possible with determination and heart. She never faltered in fighting for a fairer world, continually reminding us of our shared responsibility to build a world where everyone has the respect and dignity they deserve. Because of her — and her iconic declaration, ‘Sí, se puede ’ — nothing was impossible. Dolores changed the course of history against all odds. Through protests and marches, including the Delano grape boycott, she fundamentally reshaped California as we know it. She was more than an inspiration — though she never stopped inspiring us — she was a dear friend. Her legacy lies not just in the accomplishments she achieved, but in the people who follow in her footsteps, who take up the mantle and keep creating a better world.” U.S. Sen. Alex Padilla “Angela and I mourn the passing of Dolores Huerta, a giant in the ongoing fight for workers’ rights, women’s rights, and the protection of civil liberties. She leaves behind an enduring legacy as a civil rights and labor icon who fought tirelessly for better working conditions for migrant laborers and championed the rights of immigrants and women. From the Delano Grape Strike to her work for equal pay and reproductive freedom, Dolores fought until the end for a more just and equitable future. She showed us the power of organizing, the strength of solidarity, and what we can accomplish when we stand together. Now, it’s on all of us to carry on that torch: to keep organizing and to keep fighting.” Civil Rights 5 hours ago New Mexico Mar 19 California Attorney General Rob Bonta “Dolores Huerta was a friend, a mentor, a source of inspiration and guidance, and a lifelong hero of mine. Her activism and inspiration touched countless lives, and her ongoing legacy will surely touch countless more in the years ahead. I’m grateful she had such an influence on my own life. From my early days growing up in the headquarters of the United Farmworkers of America, to my time in public office, she was a constant, firm, irresistible force for justice and needed change. Her rallying cry “Sí Se Puede” perfectly encapsulated who she was — a woman full of fight and right who knew that if we worked together, there was nothing we couldn’t achieve. There are not enough superlatives to describe her life, legacy, and the impact she had on our nation’s ongoing pursuit of justice and fairness. She helped shape the history of the farmworkers’ movement and changed the face of the labor movement forever. She defined what it meant to own our power, use our voice, and ensure the people always remain the most potent force in our American democracy. My deepest condolences to her family. This is a devastating loss for so many in the labor movement and across the nation.” Congressman Jimmy Panetta “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers and a pioneer in the fight for labor and civil rights, women’s rights, and equality. Her lifetime of advocacy and action helped generations of farmworkers secure better wages, safer working conditions, and a voice on the job. Dolores inspired the fight for many farmworkers to achieve the American Dream and give their children a better life. Her legacy is felt well beyond our local agricultural communities on the central coast of California and throughout our country. My heart is with her family, friends, and all those who carry forward her pursuit of giving farmworkers fairness and our children a brighter future.” Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren “I’m deeply sad to hear about the passing of Dolores Huerta, a friend and legend in the farmworkers’ movement. Her work and her vision transformed our country, especially here in her home state of California. She embodied the spirit of the movement with her phrase that will live on for generations: Sí Se Puede. May she rest in peace, and may her memory be a blessing to all who loved her.” California State Sen. Scott Wiener “Today we mourn the passing of a legend who truly changed our state and our country. Throughout her 96 years, Dolores Huerta never stopped fighting to make the world a better place. Her courage and passion helped build the farmworkers movement, and she never stopped fighting for justice — whether for workers, women, LGBTQ people, immigrants, or victims of climate disasters. She energized movements, spoke truth to power, and kept fighting until the end. I had the honor of working with Dolores on various issues, including holding Big Oil accountable for climate disasters and creating an estate tax in California. Her strength, courage, and determination continually inspired me. Rest in power, my friend.” California State Sen. Jerry McNerney “I am deeply saddened by the loss of my longtime friend and ally Dolores Huerta. She was a true American legend and fierce champion of farmworkers’ rights, women’s rights, voting rights, and social and economic justice. She will be especially missed in Stockton where she grew up and attended what is now San Joaquin Delta College. To me, she was also a trusted confidante and a steadfast partner in the fight for working families. Throughout her amazing life, she changed our world for the better, not only co-founding the farmworkers’ rights movement, but also leading the labor movement, while championing women’s rights, equality for all, economic justice and so much more. Her impact was boundless. Even after receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom, her relentless energy continued to inspire generations to organize and stand up for justice. I was deeply proud and honored to know her and to be her friend. Her legacy and life’s work will never be forgotten, and the righteous causes she fought for will live on. Sí, se puede.”

headlines.title: WNBA Finals Game 6 watch party to be held at Thrive City in San Francisco
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries are one win away from being WNBA champions and will host a watch party in San Francisco on Thursday while the team plays Game 6 of the Finals in Atlanta. The Valkyries won Game 5 of the best-of-seven series 64-55 against the Atlanta Dream on Monday at Chase Center in San Francisco to go ahead 3-2 in the series and now will play Game 6 in Atlanta. Scheduling conflicts at State Farm Arena in Atlanta have prompted the WNBA to schedule Game 6 for an odd time of day on Thursday – 9:30 a.m. Pacific time, or 12:30 p.m. local time in Atlanta. The NBA’s Atlanta Hawks are moving their game there against the Cleveland Cavaliers to later Thursday night to accommodate the Valkyries-Dream game. Back in San Francisco, there will be a watch party Thursday morning at Thrive City, the plaza outside of the Chase Center arena that is home to the Valkyries and Golden State Warriors NBA team. The plaza will open to fans at 8:30 a.m. The Valkyries, founded by the same group that owns the Warriors, joined the WNBA last year and became the first expansion team in the league’s history to make the playoffs in its first season. This year, they became the first team to make the WNBA Finals in their second season. Golden State Valkyries 4 hours ago WNBA Oct 26 Kiah Stokes' big night on both ends leads Valkyries past Dream 64-55 and within a win of WNBA title

headlines.title: CSU faculty rallies continue as strike authorization vote begins
headlines.description: Rallies are taking place across California State University campuses in the Bay Area and across the state as the threat of a future strike escalates for tens of thousands of faculty members. Some rallies started before Wednesday, and almost two dozen more schools are expected to hold rallies through mid-November. Wednesday coincides with the start of a strike authorization vote for union members within the CSU system. Last week, San Jose State University union members picketed to spotlight the need for better pay so faculty and staff can keep up with a cost of living they say is a “nightmare.” Cal State East Bay also held a rally last week. San Francisco State and Sonoma State will follow Wednesday as part of almost two dozen schools that will hold rallies during the strike authorization vote period. NBC Bay Area’s Ginger Conejero Saab reports.

headlines.title: Jurors hear secret recordings in Sheng Thao corruption trial
headlines.description: Jurors heard secret recordings Wednesday in the corruption trial of former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao. Prosecutors believe the recordings help prove that David and Andy Duong, the father-and-son co-defendants, were part of a bribery and corruption scheme involving Thao and her longtime boyfriend Andre Jones, who is also a co-defendant. Jurors heard about 40 minutes of audio from board meetings at California Waste Solutions, the company owned by the Duongs. The recordings were secretly made by Cecilia Mendez, a former employee of the company. In the recordings, businessman Mario Juarez can be heard complaining to David and Andy Duong about the mayor not keeping up her end of the bargain to buy modular housing units from Evolutionary Homes, a company Juarez helped start with the Duongs. “I think it’s disappointing she’s not keeping promises,” Juarez said. “Will be problem for her re-election.” “I have long memory and I’m pretty vengeful,” Juarez said. “There’s consequences for not keeping your end of the bargain.” Sheng Thao Oct 26 Sheng Thao Oct 23 Sheng Thao Oct 22 Sheng Thao Oct 13 Prosecutors said the Duongs helped Thao get elected. In exchange, she allegedly used her position as mayor to promise to buy housing units from the Duongs, extend their recycling contract and pay her boyfriend, Andre Jones, through a job with Evolutionary Homes. The recordings also mentioned Jones asking for more money from the company. Mendez testified that she was convicted in 2019 of acting as a real estate agent without a license, grand theft and ID theft. She also testified that the federal government granted her immunity Tuesday for secretly recording the meetings in exchange for her testimony Wednesday. During cross-examination by David Duong’s attorney, Mendez testified about her close connection with Juarez, including that they shared a daughter and remained close business partners after their separation as a couple in 2005. The defense is trying to call into question the credibility of Mendez and Juarez. Juarez has already pleaded guilty for his role in the bribery and corruption scheme and is expected to testify on behalf of the government in return for a lighter sentence.

headlines.title: Even with early Game 6 tipoff, Valkyries are confident fans will find a way to watch
headlines.description: Shaunice Christmas-Miller and her wife, Kendall, have the flexibility in their jobs to work from home Thursday and watch Game 6 of the WNBA Finals despite the early tipoff on the West Coast. That doesn’t mean either is happy with the Golden State-Atlanta game starting at 9:30 a.m. PDT at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, several hours ahead of the Cavaliers-Hawks NBA game Thursday night. With the potential championship-clinching contest not being played in primetime, they know many other fans won’t be able to skip work and watch a potentially historic day in women’s basketball. Shaunice Christmas-Miller, who works in human resources, wishes everybody involved had considered the various options further in advance to avoid such last-minute scrambling. “They should have thought ahead for the whole seven-game series,” she said. “The women deserve primetime slots.” Several of the WNBA Finals games have drawn record ratings, showing how much interest there is in the league, this series and its athletes. The Valkyries have sold out every game since they began as an expansion franchise last year. “They would never make the men’s NBA final happen at 9:30 in the morning,” said Kendall Christmas-Miller, an accounting manager for a medical tech company. “I’m glad that they found accommodations but there’s still more work to be done when it comes to prioritizing women’s sports, especially when they’re performing at this level and getting the viewership.” Warriors coach Steve Kerr plans to tune in over breakfast. “We’ll have a day off that day, so, yeah, I’ll be watching,” he said. He will hardly be alone, according to Shaunice and Kendall. The couple from San Jose has attended every home playoff game this season at Chase Center — nicknamed “Ballhalla” for the raucous atmosphere created by Valkyries fans — and they believe the fan base will still show up Thursday. “Absolutely, they will definitely find a way,” Shaunice said. WNBA Oct 26 Valkyries Playoffs Oct 26 Other fans are frustrated, too “MOVE THE HAWKS GAME WOMEN = PRIME TIME” read one sign at the arena Monday night, when the Valkyries moved within a victory of a championship by beating the Dream 64-55. Others expressed their feelings on social media. Rapper Flavor Flav posted Tuesday: “Thursday is a paid holiday. Because Flavor Flav said so.” Included in his post was a photo of a note directed to bosses everywhere as a permission slip of sorts requesting excused absences for employees, signed by Flavor Flav with dual titles beneath his name — “The World’s Greatest Hype Man” and “Official Supporter of Women’s Sports.” Ole Miss women’s coach Yolett McPhee-McCuin sounded off. “I’d rather play anywhere else than have a 12:30 tip for a WNBA FINALS game man! Not a good look! For fans and for the players,” she posted on social media. “Just my 2cents that no one asked for.” Kendall Christmas-Miller said while the decision to start the game early is disappointing, “women’s sports fans are resilient and we’re going to keep pushing and keep finding a way to show up.” Valkyries focus on what they can control Golden State coach Natalie Nakase and her players have focused all along on what they can control, and this certainly isn’t one of those things. But there were some clever postgame offerings: “Call in sick, I recommend it,” point guard Veronica Burton cracked. “Yeah, right? Y’all know how to fake a cough, didn’t we all do that?” teammate Kiah Stokes added. Guard Kaila Charles has no doubt the Valkyries will adjust for the early tipoff. “I think it’s a good thing that we’re able to play in a bigger arena so that they can have more people come and support women’s basketball,” Charles said. Golden State hosting early morning watch party Valkyries co-owner Peter Guber walked into Chase Center on Monday unconcerned about the franchise’s devoted home crowd coming together when it matters most, despite the morning challenges such as commuter traffic to get into San Francisco for a watch party. Supporters have been invited to gather outside at Chase Center’s Thrive City viewing area beneath the big screen, which is 74 feet wide and 42 feet high. “Whatever they do, they come where the action is and this is the action,” Guber said, insisting Golden State’s faithful fans will all be “up and ready to go.” Nakase has made public pleas to the fan base before, and she did so again. “The beauty of Ballhalla, they’ll sacrifice,” she said. “They’re going to sacrifice. They’re going to open that app, they’re going to open their phone, they’re going to watch. I have no doubt that everyone who has been supporting us through this whole way — maybe we picked up fans within the Finals — everybody’s going to watch. … That’s what we do on Golden State, we sacrifice for the betterment of our team. “So our fans, I ain’t worried about it, our fans are going to show up, show out, we play for them because they show up, show out. They don’t ever miss a beat.” And on Thursday, even over their morning coffee. “We’ve got the best fans in the league,” Burton said, “so I’m sure they’ll be supporting us, whatever time.” ___ AP Sports Writer Pat Graham in Denver contributed to this report. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

headlines.title: Labor leader and feminist activist Dolores Huerta dies at 96
headlines.description: Labor leader and feminist activist Dolores Huerta has passed away, her family announced Wednesday. She was 96. The Latina icon spent over seven decades at the forefront of the fight for equal rights. “We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96,” her family said in a statement. “As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family. We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy.” Huerta is also remembered as being a visionary, a pioneer, courageous and resilient. When she sat down with NBC Bay Area a few years ago for an introspective look at her life, Huerta said her most valued title has been “organizer.” “You think that you’re going to go in one direction and then all of a sudden you get the calling,” Huerta previously said. “I felt that I had to help people that need to be organized so they could help themselves.” Born Dolores Clara Fernandez in Dawson, New Mexico, in 1930, advocacy was in her blood. Her father was a farmworker and union activist, while her mother was a fiercely independent entrepreneur who moved Huerta and her brothers to the San Joaquin Valley after her divorce. It was in Stockton that Huerta flourished as a girl scout, pianist and writer. But it was the racism she suffered in school that took her from her dreams to demanding. That meant launching voter registration drives, taking on grape growers and with labor unionist Cesar Chavez staging a massive boycott that would bring the “patrones,” the corporate bosses, to the negotiating table. Huerta never failed to take a position. Whether it was as a teacher in Stockton where her students struggled with hunger or in the fields of Delano where she co-founded what would become the United Farmworkers, staging strikes that changed working conditions for farmworkers in the 1960s. Huerta advocated for immigrant rights, fought against gender discrimination and redefined the role of women, wives and mothers on the picket lines. “My youngest son, Ricky, says we had to share our mother with the world, but she shared the world with us,” Huerta recalled in a previous interview with NBC Bay Area. A world that embraced one of the most iconic calls for social justice as a battle cry. Huerta’s legacy took a hit in March of 2026 when the New York Times detailed allegations that Chavez had sexually abused girls and women associated with United Farmworkers. Not long after, Huerta came forward to back Chavez’s accusers, revealing she too had been raped twice decades earlier by the revered labor leader, bearing two children she sent to live with family and friends. The damning admission dismantled Chavez’s legacy and disclosed a secret Huerta had hoped to keep forever for the sake of the movement. After a brief stint out of the public eye, Huerta returned to her calling and organizing for a future she believed, until the very end, was worth fighting for. “I believe one thing we can do is just remember we are one human family,” Huerta said in a previous interview with NBC Bay Area. “I don’t think you should use the word race unless it’s attached to the word human. We cans say we have ethnic groups and nationalities, we have cultures, but we only have one human race.” Huerta is survived by her 13 children and by the foundation that bears her name in Bakersfield. news Mar 19 California Mar 18 San Mateo County Jun 11, 2023 Dolores Huerta honored at San Mateo County Fair

headlines.title: Man charged with murder in San Francisco hit and run that killed pedestrian
headlines.description: A 29-year-old man has been charged with murder in connection with a hit-and-run collision that killed a pedestrian in San Francisco earlier this month, prosecutors announced Tuesday. David Maldonado Sanabria has been charged with murder, driving under the influence of alcohol causing injury, and leaving the scene of a crash, according to the San Francisco District Attorney’s Office. The collision occurred on the evening of Oct. 1 in the area of Moscow Street and France Avenue near the Crocker Amazon Playground. The 43-year-old man struck in the collision was taken to a hospital but succumbed to his injuries on Oct. 18, and his name has not been released by the city’s Medical Examiner’s Office. Prosecutors said that Maldonado Sanabria’s truck hit the victim, who fell backwards onto the street. Maldonado Sanabria allegedly slowed down a little, looked down at the victim, then accelerated away. He was eventually arrested and was scheduled to be arraigned Tuesday afternoon at the San Francisco Hall of Justice. The District Attorney’s Office said prosecutors are seeking to have him detained without bail pending trial. The pedestrian advocacy group Walk San Francisco last week mourned the traffic death and noted it occurred near the Crocker Amazon playground and sports fields. “The streets running along Crocker Amazon Park, plus streets around nearby Guadalupe Elementary School, are far too dangerous for pedestrians,” Walk SF executive director Jodie Medeiros said in a statement. “Too many drivers speed on these streets, and pedestrians don’t have enough protection when crossing these wide streets.”

headlines.title: Pedestrian killed, motorcyclist injured in San Jose collision
headlines.description: A pedestrian died and a motorcyclist was injured in a collision over the weekend in San Jose, police said Tuesday. On Saturday just before 1:30 a.m., a collision occurred between a male pedestrian and a man driving a motorcycle in the area of South Bascom Avenue and Fruitdale avenues. According to police, the motorcycle was going southbound on South Bascom Avenue, north of the intersection with Fruitdale Avenue, when it struck a man crossing South Bascom in an unknown direction. Both the pedestrian and the motorcyclist were taken to the hospital with life-threatening injuries. The motorcyclist was stabilized but the pedestrian died. Anyone with information on this investigation is urged to contact Detective Leslie at 4264@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-4654.

headlines.title: Fire in SF's Bernal Heights displaces 8
headlines.description: A fire in San Francisco’s Bernal Heights neighborhood early Wednesday morning displaced eight people, according to fire officials. The fire in the 900 Block of Peralta Avenue was first reported around 5:10 a.m. “Crews fought this fire for 1 hour before it was contained,” the San Francisco Fire Department said on social media. There were no reported injuries. According to the department, the displaced occupants are being assisted by the American Red Cross.
